gloss: purpose in life; reason for living; something to live for

definitions.gloss: purpose in life; reason for living; something to live for
definitions.explanation: What gives one's life meaning and makes it worth living. Can be a passion, goal, relationship, or activity that motivates someone to keep going.

examples.english: My grandchildren are my reason for living.

examples.japanese: ⟦{退職|たいしょく}→退職：04559_taishoku⟧⟦{後|ご}→〜後：noentry⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つける→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: After retirement, it's important to find a purpose in life.

examples.japanese: ⟦{音楽|おんがく}→音楽：00661_ongaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Music is what makes life worth living for him.

notes:
{生|い}き{甲斐|がい} is whatever makes a person's life feel worth living — it can be a person, an activity, or a role. Grammatically it behaves as a plain noun: X⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧ identifies what that thing is for someone. It is formed from ⟦{生|い}きる→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧ plus the 〜⟦{甲斐|かい}→甲斐：15851_kai⟧ suffix seen in ⟦やり{甲斐|がい}→やり甲斐：06653_yarigai⟧.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つける→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧ (to find one's purpose in life)
・{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧ (to feel a sense of purpose)
・{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{失|うしな}う→失う：01887_ushinau⟧ (to lose one's reason for living)
・{生|い}き{甲斐|がい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{人生|じんせい}→人生：03355_jinsei⟧ (a life with purpose)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The four-circle diagram popular in English — the overlap of ⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧ (what you love), ⟦{得意|とくい}→得意：03455_tokui⟧⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧ (what you are good at), ⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧ (what the world needs), and ⟦{稼|かせ}げる→稼ぐ：02040_kasegu⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧ (what you can be paid for) — is a foreign elaboration. In ordinary Japanese use the word is far humbler and carries no requirement that the thing be productive or paid: a grandchild or a garden qualifies.

WRITING NOTE:
Often written いきがい in hiragana. The word has been borrowed into English as 'ikigai,' usually in the four-circle sense rather than the everyday Japanese one.
